issues.description: PR conflates three unrelated changes: POST tests, README reformat, and FAQ entry.
issues.detail: Stated scope is adding POST tests for things_advanced, but the diff also sweeps the README (signature reorder, status formatting, bounded_stream swap) and adds a new FAQ section. Reviewing is harder than it should be. Split into separate PRs so the test addition lands cleanly and the README rewrite gets its own justification.

issues.description: README handle() signature reordered to (req, resp, ex, params) without justification.
issues.detail: The README now declares handle(req, resp, ex, params) where it previously had (ex, req, resp, params). This is an undocumented drive-by API-shape change in a PR titled 'add POST tests.' Either justify it in the commit message with a versionchanged note or drop it; readers copying the example will hit broken handlers.

issues.description: Switching req.stream to req.bounded_stream in the example is unexplained and contradicts the PR description.
issues.detail: The PR description claims it adds req.content_length to req.stream.read(), but the diff actually swaps to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different semantics under WSGI when Content-Length is wrong or absent, and this is the change that makes the new 400 test pass. Name it, document why bounded_stream is correct, add a one-line comment.

issues.description: FAQ example is more elaborate than the lesson it teaches and has poor taste.
issues.detail: The lesson is 'how to set headers in tests,' but PostTest layers Content-Length checks, nested if/else, and three status codes. Strip to one handler that reads stream and returns 400 on empty body, with flat branches. FAQ code gets copied; write what you'd want a beginner to imitate.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert, a Python footgun.
issues.detail: `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken `assert(x, y)` tuple form. Write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`. Small, but FAQ code is canonical reference material.

issues.description: New tests assert status codes only and duplicate header dicts instead of naming invariants.
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 share Authorization and Content-Type and assert 201/400 with no docstring naming the property under test. Pull common headers into a base dict so the one meaningful difference (empty body with Content-Length: 1) is obvious, and add a comment stating the invariant being tested.

synthesis.summary: Panel verdict: NEEDS-WORK due to scope creep, not correctness. The actual test additions are useful, but this PR smuggles three patches into one: tests, a sweeping README reformat (including an undocumented handle() signature reorder), and a new FAQ entry with over-elaborate example code. The bounded_stream swap is the real semantic fix and contradicts the PR description, yet it gets no comment. Split the PR, justify the README changes, simplify the FAQ example, and name invariants in the new tests.
